notes: Resident population from the 2024 Iraqi census by qadaa (district) — Baghdad governorate's 10 qadaas (Karkh, Rusafa, Adhamiya, Sadr City 1&2, Zawraa, Kadhimiya, Abu Ghraib, Madain, Mahmudiyah) function as real intra-city districts here, each with its own published population; districts only partially inside the map's bounding box are linearly prorated by the fraction of their area inside the box (an area-based approximation, not a building-density-weighted one). No real employment/workplace census exists: total jobs per district are estimated as a flat 40% of that district's resident population, then spread across OSM buildings weighted by floor area alone (no building-type distinction, no calibration to any real workplace statistic). Home-work commute flows are generated by an unconstrained gravity model (distance-decay exponent 1.8, 3km minimum trip distance) — there is no real origin-destination data, measured or estimated, informing these flows in either direction. — Reviewer refinement (2026-08-18): granularity scored adm3, not adm4 — qadaa is formally ADM2 in Iraq's hierarchy (the guide's ADM2 examples include the UA raion, its direct analogue) while functioning here as intra-city districts of ~800k people each; per §2 rule 3 the middle grain is recorded with bounds (adm4 by function / adm2 by hierarchy).
sources: cosit.gov.iq (Iraq Central Statistical Organisation, 2024 general census, results published Nov 2025)
